chapter: Hightower: New Orleans parades and early players
title: Freddie Keppard and ragtime
summary: He calls Keppard among the greatest, playing ragtime, which was all Scott Joplin before it was called jazz.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Yeah, that's what they used to advertise. Yeah, that's right. In a puncture wagon, horse and wagon. And he never was no more good. He'd take him sick and they'd take him to the hospital. There was no good. And shortly after that, he died. But I didn't realize, but they said, after Freddie come up and started playing, they said, we tried to say Freddie was great, but they said he was the greatest one that there was. Bowling. Bowling, that's right. He was the greatest. He could make the highest notes.
You think Freddie Keppert was about the greatest you ever remember hearing though now?
Yeah. That is for playing ragtime music.

Yeah, rag, we didn't call it no jazz then. You see, because everything was Scott Joplin then. Yeah. See, and we played all, any time any musician could play Scott Joplin's, I've got the books. I have the books. There's twelve numbers in the books, isn't there? Well every one of Scott Joplin's numbers, from Maple Leaf Ray to Cascade, and any musician, any trumpet player could play Cascade, he was a musician of mine.
And that's what Freddie Keppert played.
Would you like Keppert better than Joe Oliver?
